The loop is `for tr in [(p1,o1), (p2,o2), ...]: g.add((w20, tr[0], tr[1]))` -- syntactically add_in_loop, but every item shares the SAME fixed subject w20 and the predicates are ad hoc / heterogeneous (rdf:type twice, then rdfs:label, skos:definition, dcterms:source, skos:scopeNote, skos:note, ipo:coversLearningObjective), not a homogeneous row schema. This is RDF-semantically a single-subject property bundle (the add_run_shared_subject idiom), not row-shaped data, so it is translated as one grouped +{ w20 p1 o1 ; p2 o2 ; ... } with no loop and no `for @bindings`, rather than reshaping each (p,o) pair into a {"p":...,"o":...} binding row and templating a variable predicate ?p -- which would force a mapping shape onto data that has none. Classified minor-restructuring because the Python for-loop itself is eliminated, even though the RDF payload (same 8 triples on the same subject) is untouched.

Contrast with the sibling region altunelyusuf__SemanticTechnologies__...build_core_v5_3_0.py__<module>_147 in this same repository, whose loop DOES vary the subject per row over a homogeneous named-field schema (pid/plab/pdef/prange) and was correctly translated with `for @bindings in` -- the two loops look alike at the surface (a Python for over a list of tuples calling g.add) but differ exactly on the property that decides which idiom fits: whether the subject and predicate shape are per-row data or a fixed one-off bundle.
